children: Oil prices surged after Saudi Arabia shut down a pipeline that had served as a crucial outlet for crude amid the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, which was trading at around $104 a barrel before the closure, climbed above $107. Analysts said the price could move higher if the closure, which followed drone strikes by Iran-aligned militants in Iraq, drags on.

"The relatively contained price reaction suggests the market still expects Saudi inventories to cushion exports in the near term, but if the disruption extends beyond the five-to-seven-day inventory cushion, that could change quickly," Rystad Energy analyst Janiv Shah wrote in a note Monday.
